ai.title: Population Demography
ai.subject: Public health
ai.summary: Demography studies population size, structure and dynamics to guide health planning. It informs disease burden, resource allocation and intervention targeting in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: Demography is the quantitative study of human populations, covering size, density, distribution, age, sex, fertility, mortality and migration. It uses census data, surveys and vital statistics.
Not applicable – demography is descriptive, not a disease entity.
Population changes arise from birth rates, death rates, migration and policy. In East Africa, high fertility, HIV, malaria and migration shape demographics.
Demographic data appear as tables, graphs and indices such as the demographic transition model, age‑specific mortality rates and population pyramids.
Data collection methods and their interpretation.
